paper_id: CLMTracing_ Black-box User-level Watermarking for Code Language Model Tracing__oa_W4416255597
title: CLMTracing: Black-box User-level Watermarking for Code Language Model Tracing
motivation: Open-source code LMs on platforms like Hugging Face face unauthorized commercial exploitation and redistribution, requiring user-level tracing for enforcement.
problem_framing: Black-box watermarking for user-level code LM tracing requires simultaneously ensuring harmlessness, robustness, and efficient embedding with minimal samples.
key_insight: Redundant parameters in code LMs can be repurposed to store watermarks while preserving model utility, and selective parameter updates resistant to fine-tuning.
method_signature: Rule-based watermark + utility-preserving injection with SRW parameter selection + adversarial training for black-box embedding.
evaluation_criteria: WSR (effectiveness), pass@all (harmlessness), robustness against fine-tuning and detection attacks.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Random method sometimes slightly outperforms SRW because regularization samples do not consistently improve performance and even cause drops.
thinking_moves: Reframe model tracing as parameter-level poisoning with utility preservation constraints
Exploit redundancy in code LMs by targeting only parameters with high watermark relevance and low performance relevance
Enhance robustness through adversarial perturbations that prepare watermark to adapt to parameter shifts
Aggregate multiple degradation metrics (pass@all) to resolve contradictory conclusions across different k values
